**Finding submitted: deviation (EXCLUSIVITY), preferred-level redline.**

What I inspected:
- **sec-2 (License/Hosting)** — §2(a) (p0022) grants us a *non-exclusive* licence and expressly says we are "not obligated to utilize the License" and are free to use similar third-party software and services: this benefits us and was left untouched.
- **sec-3(i) Credit Bureau Information (p0042)** — the operative problem: "Client **shall order** TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface" — a 100%-of-requirements tie for that category.
- **sec-5 / sec-6 (compensation, p0044–p0047)**, **sec-8 (Client covenants)**, **sec-7**, **sec-10**, **sec-12/13/14** — no other exclusivity binding us; §8(d)'s Credit Data licence to TrueLink is expressly *nonexclusive*, and §13 (p0078) shows the term auto-renews for successive one-year periods.

Why it fails the fallback: only "defined product category" is met. The tie runs for the initial term and every automatic renewal (so not capped at 12 months), and nothing terminates it automatically on TrueLink's service-level or delivery/transmission failures — full-term exclusive dealing without a performance-based exit. §14's ~one-month termination right is a mitigant but requires abandoning the whole service.

Redline (validated, ok:true): one surgical replace in p0042 — "shall order" → "may, but is not required to, order from" — removing the sole-supplier obligation while preserving TrueLink's transmission duty and disclaimer, with the 12-month/performance-exit fallback offered in the comment.
